item.title: Bitwave Year in Review: Celebrating 2025
item.author: Amy Kalnoki
item.content:encoded:
# Bitwave Year in Review: Celebrating 2025
As 2025 comes to a close, we're reflecting on a year that redefined what's possible for on-chain finance.
2025 saw the digital asset industry hit new highs for market sentiment, enterprise adoption, and legislative favor. New conversations started to gather steam, especially around bringing institutions on-chain and stablecoin-powered B2B payments. Bitwave helped lead those conversations at major industry events, on stage at EDAS, and online with our partners on webinars. But that's not all! We also supercharged our platform to meet this moment head-on.
Below is a look back at what we achieved together this year.
## Events & Bitwave Thought Leadership
2025 was a milestone year for bringing B2B payments onchain and for bringing enterprise finance and real-world blockchain operations to the forefront of the financial services industry. This year, Bitwave hosted several important industry events and provided key thought leadership in the space. Here is a round-up of a few of our most popular events of the year.
### **Onchain B2B Payments Day at ETH Denver**
**‍**We kicked off the year by taking over ETHDenver, with a groundbreaking event co-hosted alongside Deloitte, NetSuite, Aleo, and PayPal. This full-day program showcased how [on-chain payments](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/b2b-payments-are-broken-heres-how-blockchain-fixes-them), transparency, and automation are reshaping corporate finance and treasury operations.
### **Stablecoin Payments House at Consensus **
**‍**Together with Aleo and Ripple, we [advanced the dialogue](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/the-future-of-finance-on-display-at-the-stablecoin-payments-house) around privacy, compliance, and scale in stablecoin payments.
### **Enterprise Digital Asset Summit (EDAS)**
**‍**Our flagship summit returned bigger than ever, officially *sold out* during San Francisco Tech Week! EDAS 2025 featured [our most expansive agenda and speaker lineup yet,](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/top-5-themes-edas-2025) hitting everything from stablecoin payments to agentic AI in back-office finance, and cementing EDAS as the must-attend enterprise blockchain event.
![Image](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64c568d103c4e2da8755c388/6949eae2fb07c015e57b24d7_amy-caitlyn.jpg)
### [Money 20/20 ](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/ripple-bitwave-stablecoin-payments-partnership)
[[Ripple-Bitwave Stablecoin Payments Partnership](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/ripple-bitwave-stablecoin-payments-partnership)**‍**Bitwave continued bridging TradFi and DeFi, appearing alongside leaders from Ripple, Blockdaemon, and Canton Network for two different events to drive the future of compliant financial infrastructure.
### **Webinar Series**
This year's education and enablement initiatives included several deep-dive webinar series.
* [Bitwave + Arbitrum](https://university.bitwave.io/bundles/arbitrum-bitwave) was our first Spanish-language webinar talking yield-bearing stablecoins, TGE tax considerations, and a limited edition CPE NFT * [Bitwave + Polymesh](https://university.bitwave.io/courses/institutional-finance-on-chain-compliance-accounting) talked about tokenization for institutions and bringing private markets on-chain. * [Bitwave + AICPA](https://university.bitwave.io/courses/aicpa-stablecoin-reporting-criteria) focused on unpacking the work of the Attestation Subgroup to draw up the Stablecoin Reporting Criteria and Stablecoin Controls Exposure Draft
### Case Studies & Customer Insights
We highlighted the transformative work of [FV Bank](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/fv-bank-redefines-institutional-grade-client-and-tax-reporting-efficiency-with-bitwave), demonstrating how institutions can redefine client and tax reporting efficiency using Bitwave.
![Image](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64c568d103c4e2da8755c388/6949ebce4024b58828b32ea2_payments-day.jpg)
## Another Year Making Waves EVERYWHERE
2025 took the Bitwave team across the world to connect with customers, regulators, partners, and innovators pushing enterprise blockchain forward.
We spent a lot of time in New York this year, hitting Digital Asset Summit NY, Permissionless, the WSBA Crypto & Blockchain Summit, and The Bridge.
But if you missed us there, you could find us…everywhere else. From Zurich for Point Zero Forum, Cannes for ETHCC, Rio for **Stellar Meridian**, Toronto for Consensus, and finally bringing it back to the states for SuiteWorld in Las Vegas, 2025 was another year of our unofficial slogan: Bitwave is everywhere.
Our founders and executives were featured across top global stages, continuing to lead the conversation around compliance, payments, and enterprise adoption.
### **Pat White, Bitwave CEO**‍
• Stablecoin House at ETH CC : Debuted SRIP, the new protocol standard for on-chain, cross-chain, and off-chain remittance advice. • SoDA Symposium • [Market Mover: The Opening Bell](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=scDDahBvN_M)
### Amy Kalnoki, Bitwave COO
• Featured on [Currency LIVE](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/amy-kalnoki-on-why-enterprises-must-embrace-onchain-finance-today) with BVNK and on Subscript's “[Diving Deep](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nOO2wvBFVt8)” podcast • Panelist at [BVNK's Summer Social ](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7375907974076116992)with Modern Treasury and Highnote
![Image](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64c568d103c4e2da8755c388/6949eb839053ac5240579828_bitwave-award.jpg)
## Recognition & Awards: Leading the Industry
This year brought meaningful validation for Bitwave's leadership, technology, and industry contribution.
### Stellar Community Fund Award
We were honored to receive an award from the Stellar Development Foundation to extend our enterprise capabilities with new [Stellar-based custodial and on-chain payment solutions](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/bitwave-stellar-enabling-custodial-on-chain-payments-for-enterprises), building on our July launch of native Stellar integration.
### Market Maps & Thought Leadership Recognitions
* The Tie's report on the [Privacy Imperative for Stablecoin Payments](https://www.thetie.io/insights/research/the-canton-network-series-part-3-of-5/) * Named an Enterprise & B2B Leader on the [Stablecoin Market Map](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/stablecoin-market-map/) from CB Insights & Stablecon * Highlighted in Stableguide by Stabledash for our stablecoin AR/AP workflow
### Featured Application on Canton Network
[This designation](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/bitwave-named-a-gsf-featured-app) recognizes Bitwave as one of the applications actively advancing institutional-grade on-chain finance.
![Image](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64c568d103c4e2da8755c388/6949eb47a3a3f134b04737f8_three-pillars.jpg)
## **Continuing to Innovate on What We Do Best**
Bitwave's crypto subledger is the industry leader, but even with that distinction, we never stop improving our core product. In 2025, we delivered some of our most impactful product expansions yet, giving enterprises even more workflows, reports, automation, and visibility into the digital asset data.
The Bitwave of today is the platform of choice to help you:
### **Move Money Faster With Confidence**
* Pay hundreds of vendors in a single workflow using stablecoin-first enterprise payments in Bitwave * Execute payments for invoices synced from NetSuite and QuickBooks, with built-in compliance, such as penny testing and wallet verification * Operate flexibly across custodial and self-custodial wallets, with seamless fiat on- and off-ramps
### **Close Faster and Reduce Accounting Friction in Bitwave**
* Gain a clear, collaborative view of the close process with our new Close Dashboard * Handle high-volume activity efficiently through in-place rollups and ERP-ready journal entries * Resolve issues faster with clearer audit trails, review states, and exception handling
### **Handle Complex Inventory and Pricing with Precision**
* Manage multi-currency subsidiaries, reallocations, and complex inflows/outflows with greater control * Preserve accounting accuracy through cost basis carry-forward and reference runs * Apply flexible pricing rules by wallet or transaction, tailored for reporting, revaluation, and revenue recognition
### **Track DeFi Activity Like Any Other Financial Operation**
* Monitor lending, borrowing, and LP positions in one unified view * Track accruals and rewards over time, bringing DeFi activity into standard financial workflows
### **Securely Operate at Enterprise Scale**
* Support complex organizational structures with full multi-currency subsidiary support * Retain control over sensitive data with Bring Your Own Keys (BYOK) and encryption stacking * Work more efficiently in a refreshed Bitwave interface designed for day-to-day finance teams
### **Expand Coverage Across Chains, Validators, and Systems**
* Accurately account for Solana validator operations, including commissions, rewards, and vote transactions * Integrate enterprise ERPs like Oracle Fusion and SAP, including SFTP-based workflows * Gain broader blockchain coverage with new and enhanced integrations across Canton, Polymesh, Dexalot, Avalanche, Aptos, and faster EVM syncing * Strengthen exchange and custodian connectivity with expanded support for Coinbase Pro, BitGo, and Foundry
### **Bring All Financial Data Together**
* Ingest data flexibly via spreadsheets, data warehouses, and custom pipelines * Reconcile on-chain and off-chain activity using richer transaction, wallet, and balance feeds built for institutional scale.
Whew, that's a lot!
![Image](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64c568d103c4e2da8755c388/6949ea3547523891b4337e02_payments-at-bitwave.jpg)
## **What about 2026?**
As we look ahead, the momentum for this industry is undeniable. In 2026, we expect to see:
* Acceleration of stock tokenization**, **, blurring the line between equities and tokens. * 24/7 trading become the global default** **for digital-first markets. * The first real supply-chain blockchain use cases are entering production**,**, driven by transparency requirements.
## **A Big Thank You!**
To all of our customers, partners, and community, thank you! Thank you for your business, collaboration, and feedback this year. Bitwave continues to grow because of your partnership.
Cheers to a remarkable 2025! We look forward to working with you in 2026.

item.title: The Engineering Reality of Stablecoin Integration at Neobanks
item.author: Pat White
item.content:encoded:
# The Engineering Reality of Stablecoin Integration at Neobanks
> Neobanks are racing to offer stablecoins, but the real challenge isn't custody—it's accounting. Here's what the infrastructure actually requires.
If you're running a neobank in 2026 and you don't have a stablecoin strategy, your board is probably asking why not. If you do have a stablecoin strategy, your finance team is probably asking why you thought this was a good idea.
The appeal is obvious. Your customers want to hold USDC. Your competitors are announcing crypto features. The regulatory fog is lifting—the GENIUS Act just removed payment stablecoins from securities regulation. And the economics are compelling: 80% lower fees than wire transfers, instant settlement, 24/7 operation.
So you build the customer-facing features. The wallet interface looks great. The onboarding flow is smooth. You integrate with a custody provider. You launch.
Then your controller tries to close the books and discovers that blockchain transactions settle in seconds but reconciliation still takes days. That your ERP doesn't handle 18-decimal-place precision. That cross-chain transfers create duplicate accounting entries. That "transaction hash 0x7f3b..." means nothing to your general ledger.
The technology for moving money works beautifully. The technology for accounting for that money movement? That's the hard part.
![three-headed-infrastructure-monster.jpg](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64c568d103c4e2da8755c388/691e3a4336fb729c202cce15_three-headed-infrastructure-monster.jpg)
## The Three-Headed Infrastructure Monster
Implementing stablecoins isn't just about choosing which blockchain to support or which custody provider to use. The real challenge is unglamorous back-office work that nobody talks about at conferences.
![stablecoin-implementation-challenges.png](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64c568d103c4e2da8755c388/691e3a80e4c575f1948aa4ec_stablecoin-implementation-challenges.png)
### The Reconciliation Challenge
Traditional finance operates in batch mode. Banks process transactions during business hours and reconcile overnight. Blockchain operates 24/7, with transactions confirming in seconds.
Each blockchain has its own transaction structure, timing, and cost model. The complexity multiplies across chains. Ethereum gas fees work differently than Solana.
Then there's the internal transfer problem. When you bridge assets between chains, you get a sent transaction on one chain and a receipt transaction on another. Your accounting system sees two transactions. It's one movement. Fail to collapse these, and you're double-counting everything.
Without automated mapping from on-chain data to accounting records, your finance team becomes human middleware. Manual reconciliation will never catch up.
### The Book of Record Problem
Traditional ERPs handle two decimal places.
Blockchain transactions use 16, 18, or even 36 decimal places. This mismatch creates inaccurate accounting if you round. At scale, those errors compound into material misstatements.
You need [a crypto-specific subledger](https://www.bitwave.io/solutions/crypto-subledger) that handles crypto natively and integrates with both blockchain and traditional ERPs. It needs to support various cost basis methodologies—GAAP and tax books simultaneously. It needs real-time balance tracking across wallets, exchanges, and custodians. And it needs audit trails that satisfy both traditional auditors and blockchain compliance requirements.
### The Core Ledger Integration Gap
A blockchain transaction hash means nothing to your accounting software. Without ERP integration, crypto accounting becomes a parallel workflow, disconnected from your chart of accounts. Your controllers maintain two sets of books and manually bridge the gap at month-end.
You need to turn on-chain transactions into journal entries with correct GL mappings, cost centers, and entity codes. Multi-entity structures and FX calculations need to work automatically. Your existing approval workflows must be preserved too.
**These three challenges compound.** You can't solve reconciliation without a proper subledger. You can't maintain a subledger without ERP integration. And you can't integrate with your ERP without solving reconciliation. This is why most neobanks partner rather than build.
To understand what solving these challenges requires, let's walk through each infrastructure layer, using[ Bitwave's architecture](https://www.bitwave.io/solutions/crypto-subledger) as a reference. Bitwave processes billions in stablecoin transactions for enterprises including Coinbase.
## What the Solution Looks Like
![five-layer-stablecoin-infrastructure.png](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64c568d103c4e2da8755c388/691e3aa0a0523cd06db97306_five-layer-stablecoin-infrastructure.png)
### Data Ingestion Layer
The foundation is data ingestion. You need to connect to multiple blockchains—not just Ethereum, but Layer 2s like Polygon, Arbitrum, and Base, plus alternative L1s like Solana and Stellar.
Then there are exchange integrations. Major platforms need connections to Coinbase, Binance, Kraken, Gemini, and dozens of others. You need custodial wallet support for Fireblocks, BitGo, Anchorage, and NYDIG. For customers doing anything beyond basic transfers, you need DeFi protocol monitoring for platforms like Aave, Uniswap, Compound, and MakerDAO.
Transaction detection at scale is its own engineering challenge. You're not just pulling data—you're classifying it, detecting patterns, and identifying transaction types in real-time across heterogeneous systems.
**How Bitwave Handles This**
Bitwave provides comprehensive blockchain coverage from L1s like Bitcoin and Ethereum to L2s and sidechains like Arbitrum, Hedera, Base, and Polygon. The platform supports [over 200 blockchains, exchanges, custodians, and DeFi protocols](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/best-crypto-accounting-software-10-must-have-features-part-2) with automated data ingestion.
### The Subledger Architecture
Once you're ingesting data from 200+ sources, you need to normalize it into a coherent accounting system.
The subledger sits between blockchain chaos and your traditional ERP, acting as a translation layer. It handles transaction normalization across chains, turning wildly different data structures into standardized accounting events.
Automatic categorization is critical. Is this revenue? An expense? An asset transfer? An internal movement? The platform needs[ mechanisms to detect and collapse internal transfers](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/multi-chain-reconciliation-platforms) so you don't double-count cross-chain swaps and wallet-to-wallet moves.
Cost basis tracking gets complex quickly. You need to support multiple methodologies—FIFO, LIFO, specific lot identification, weighted average. Different jurisdictions and tax strategies require different approaches.
And crucially, you need to handle those 18+ decimal places natively. No rounding. No precision loss. No material misstatements compounding over thousands of transactions.
**How Bitwave Handles This**
Bitwave is [purpose-built as a crypto subledger](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/bitwave-best-market-leading-subledger-ethereum-bitcoin-accounting), integrating directly with ERPs like NetSuite, QuickBooks, and Sage Intacct. The platform [supports various cost basis methodologies](https://www.bitwave.io/solutions/crypto-subledger) , maintaining different books — GAAP and tax — simultaneously. It provides [enterprise-grade compliance](https://www.bitwave.io/compliance-and-auditability) with GAAP, IFRS, and jurisdiction-specific tax treatments.
### Reconciliation Engine
With normalized data in your subledger, you need continuous reconciliation between on-chain activity and accounting records.
The real-time versus batch processing trade-off is crucial. Traditional accounting reconciles at month-end. For stablecoin operations, real-time reconciliation means your internal accounting records update instantly as transactions confirm on-chain. It's continuous, automatic synchronization across multiple blockchains, tokens, and vendor wallets.
You need to handle edge cases: failed transactions that consumed gas fees, stuck transactions, transaction replacements, and chain reorganizations. Multi-wallet and multi-entity reconciliation adds complexity when operating globally.
Segregation of duties matters for compliance. Different users need different roles and responsibilities within the platform, allowing them to reconcile transactions categorized in different ways. One user reconciles accounts receivable, another handles accounts payable.
**How Bitwave Handles This**
Bitwave provides [real-time reconciliation](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/real-time-reconciliation-reporting-for-stablecoin-payouts-2025-guide) where internal accounting records update instantly as transactions confirm on-chain. The platform [automates reconciliation](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/multi-chain-reconciliation-platforms) across multiple blockchains, wallets, and exchanges, including internal transfers, bridging, staking, and NFT/DeFi activity. It [automatically categorizes complex DeFi activity](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/reconciling-defi-transactions-at-scale) including swaps, staking, liquidity provision, and bridges.
### ERP Integration Layer
The final layer connects your crypto subledger to your traditional ERP. This is where most build-it-yourself projects fail. It's not enough to generate journal entries—you need proper mappings, multi-entity structures, and existing control frameworks.
Direct API connections to leading platforms are essential. Integration with QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, and Xero needs to be native, not a CSV import hack. Journal entry generation needs proper GL codes, cost centers, entity codes, and all the metadata your controllers need.
Two-way sync is critical for data integrity. When you mark an invoice as paid in your ERP, that flows back to your crypto system. When a payment executes on-chain, that updates your payables in real-time.
The audit trail needs to provide granular detail required for stringent audit processes.
**How Bitwave Handles This**
Bitwave acts as a subledger that generates journal entries for crypto transactions and pushes them to platforms like Sage Intacct. Bitwave is an [official marketplace partner](http://bitwave.io/integrations) of QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage, and Xero. [Journal entries flow automatically](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/real-time-reconciliation-reporting-for-stablecoin-payouts-2025-guide) into your general ledger with correct GL accounts, cost centers, and entity codes, with multi-entity structures and FX calculations working out of the box.
### The Payment Layer
Infrastructure isn't complete without payment execution. This is where you actually move stablecoins to vendors, customers, and partners.
Vendor wallet verification is non-negotiable. You need built-in wallet verification to track and manage payments, with allow-list wallets and addresses for end-to-end security.
Batch payment capabilities are essential for operational efficiency. Your AP team shouldn't make individual transactions. They need to select multiple invoices, verify wallets against your allow-list, and execute bulk payments across tokens and blockchains in one operation.
Integration with custody providers is critical for security. Instead of managing private keys and hot wallets, enterprises can connect to existing custodial solutions like Coinbase Prime. This provides institutional-grade security while maintaining the speed and cost benefits of stablecoin payments.
**How Bitwave Handles This**
Bitwave delivers the [first enterprise-ready stablecoin payments platform](https://www.bitwave.io/solutions/stablecoin-b2b-payments-enterprise-ar-ap) built for finance teams, with the [Bitwave Payment Network](https://www.bitwave.io/blog/bitwave-announces-the-future-of-on-chain-b2b-payments-the-bitwave-payment-network) allowing payers to create and manage vendor payments in ETH, BTC, or stablecoins while vendors receive accurate, invoice-backed payments and finance teams automate GL entries. Every payment is tracked and reconciled with complete audit visibility, and vendor wallet changes require explicit approval with immutable audit trails.
## Your Core Competency is Banking, Not Maintaining Crypto Infrastructure
The neobanks winning with stablecoins aren't the ones with the best blockchain engineers. They're the ones who made smart build-versus-partner decisions and got to market quickly with reliable, compliant systems.
Even companies like Coinbase, who arguably have more crypto engineering expertise than anyone, rely on Bitwave to move millions in vendor payments.
With Bitwave, you get battle-tested compliance and audit processes. With Bitwave you get audit-ready bookkeeping that businesses from Fortune 100 titans to early-stage crypto-native projects trust. Building equivalent compliance capabilities from scratch is expensive and risky. Your core competency is banking, not maintaining crypto infrastructure.
Ready to explore stablecoin infrastructure for your neobank?[ Contact Bitwave](https://www.bitwave.io/request-a-demo) for a technical consultation.
